build_inputs.aarch64_config:
# Repository build profile for the aarch64 AEAD path.
#
# This file sits at the repository root, not under `core/`, because cargo
# discovers `.cargo/config.toml` by walking up from the **current working
# directory**. The repository's prescribed commands run from this root with
# `--manifest-path core/Cargo.toml`, which never looks inside `core/.cargo/`, so
# the flags used to be silently absent from exactly the builds that matter.
# It is scoped by target cfg, so x86_64 and every other target are untouched.
#
# Why these flags exist at all: the native transport negotiates AES-GCM wherever
# its backend can be accelerated (`aes`/`polyval`/`ghash` gate their ARMv8
# backends on the `aes_armv8`/`polyval_armv8` cfgs, which only a global flag can
# set, and the AES/PMULL instructions additionally need the target features).
# On `aarch64-apple-darwin` the `aes` and `sha2` target features are already the
# target's defaults, so the two cfgs are the half a host build would miss; on
# `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` the baseline declares only `neon`, so the codegen
# flags are needed there too. Hence all four, everywhere.
#
# Measured consequence of losing them (same source, same machine, same protocol):
# 214 MiB/s against 802 MiB/s on one stream, 425 against 1556 MiB/s on two.
# `core/crates/layerfs-bridge` now refuses to compile for aarch64 without this
# profile instead of silently negotiating the ChaCha20-Poly1305 fallback.
#
# These are the crates' own documented cfg knobs plus the ARMv8 target features,
# not patches. An explicit RUSTFLAGS environment variable overrides this table, so
# a scripted or container build that sets RUSTFLAGS must repeat these flags.
#
# The reference workspace under `crates/` has no `aes`/`polyval`/`ghash` in its
# lockfile, so these flags change nothing for it.
[target.'cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")']
rustflags = [
    "--cfg", "aes_armv8",
    "--cfg", "polyval_armv8",
    "--cfg", "chacha20_force_neon",
    "-C", "target-feature=+aes,+sha2",
]
# `rustdoc` inherits neither the flags above nor a `rustdocflags` table in a
# cfg-formed target (verified on cargo 1.85.1: the rustdoc command line carries
# neither), so the bridge's build-time refusal exempts documentation builds
# (`not(doc)`) in the crate itself. A doc build produces no binary, and every
# build that does still requires this profile.
build_inputs.rustc:
rustc 1.85.1 (4eb161250 2025-03-15)
binary: rustc
commit-hash: 4eb161250e340c8f48f66e2b929ef4a5bed7c181
commit-date: 2025-03-15
host: aarch64-apple-darwin
release: 1.85.1
LLVM version: 19.1.7
build_inputs.cargo:
cargo 1.85.1 (d73d2caf9 2024-12-31)
release: 1.85.1
commit-hash: d73d2caf9e41a39daf2a8d6ce60ec80bf354d2a7
